jobs.occupation: Ph.D. student (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholds (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (26.2878 hours/week = 66%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1Ph.D. student (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholdsThe work of the chair of experimental physics 1 focuses on basic research: Oneof the most essential elements of todays education and research is to gain abetter understanding of the structure of matter and the fundamental principles ofnature. In this process the basic research of physics plays an important role as itprovides a base for technical innovations and development. Hadron Physicsdeals with strong interacting particles consisting of quarks and gluons. Amongthose hadrons also rank the building blocks of the atomic nucleus, the protonand the neutron. There are many other hadrons that can only be created viacollisions of high energetic particles in big particle accelerators. The created hadrons are detected by modern and complex detectors to examine their composition and interactions.The position is embedded in two research programs. DEMOS ("Democratizing Models") is an ErUM research initiative developing a federated, interoperable standard for describing, sharing and re-evaluating physics models across particle, hadron, nuclear, neutrino and astroparticle physics. Hadronic coupled-channel amplitudes are one of its flagship applications: they are analytically intricate and rarely reproducible from the publication alone, which makes them an ideal test case for the new standard. HADRON 2030 is an intercollaborative research network dedicated to studies of hadron physics. Within the ExHAT (Exploration of Heavy Hadrons at Thresholds) project, we will explore heavy hadrons at thresholds using spectroscopy methods with LHCb data and inclusive production studies with ALICE. The flagship case is the doubly charmed tetraquark Tcc(3875)+, which lies a fraction of an MeV below the D0D*+ threshold. Line shape, pole position, three-body DD-pi dynamics and isospin breaking have to be disentangled in a joint effort of theory and experiment.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 3 yearsStart: at the earliest possible dateApply by:  2026-11-15Your tasks:- Application of advanced methods of data selection, efficiency and resolutionstudies within LHCb data analysis.- Construction, fitting and analytic continuation of coupled-channel scatteringamplitudes.- Decipherment and serialization of the complex amplitudes in the DEMOS / amplitude-serialization format.- Collaboration within the DEMOS / HADRON 2030 networks.- Exchange with the experimental collaborations [LHCb, BESIII, Belle II, GlueX, ...] and with EFT/lattice QCD groups.Your profile:- Master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, completed by the starting date.- Background in experimental particle physics or hadron physics, and familiarity with quantum field theory and scattering theory.- Good scientific programming skills (Julia, Python or C++) and experience with version control and reproducible workflows.- Very good command of written and spoken English.- Interest in working at the interface between theory and experiment and inopen, reusable research software.https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA)

Company DescriptionAbout usPassion for food. Hunger for tech. We make METRO digital.Today technology is driving the world. And at METRO.digital we are driving the technology for one of the leading international wholesalers specializing in food - METRO. From e-commerce to checkout, to delivery software, we work on a wide range of products to make each day a success for our customers and colleagues. With passion and ownership, we build the future of wholesale.Are you striving to create smart solutions for customers around the globe? You want to grow in a flexible environment? Let the right career opportunity find you and join us!Job DescriptionThe LUCA programLUCA is METRO’s strategic SAP S/4HANA Finance transformation program. It safeguards business continuity and addresses security and compliance risks while enabling greater standardization, harmonization and centralization across Finance. Alongside new-country rollouts, the program continuously evolves and supports the productive solution used by countries already live on LUCA.Purpose of the roleBased in Düsseldorf, Germany, the SAP Finance Project Manager will lead the delivery of change projects for LUCA countries already operating on the productive SAP S/4HANA Finance solution. Typical assignments include the implementation of new electronic-invoicing mandates, other legal and regulatory requirements, and business-driven changes that affect Finance processes, integrations, data, controls and operational procedures.The role is designed for an experienced SAP Financials professional who has moved into project coordination and delivery management. The Project Manager must understand Finance requirements and SAP solution implications well enough to structure work, challenge plans, connect the correct experts and drive decisions, while remaining accountable for scope, schedule, budget, quality, risk and stakeholder alignment in a large international SAP landscape.Your responsibilitiesEnd-to-end project delivery- Own the delivery of assigned SAP Finance projects for LUCA live countries from initiation and scoping through design, build, testing, deployment, hypercare and closure.- Translate legal, regulatory and business change requests into structured projects with clear objectives, scope boundaries, deliverables, milestones, governance, resource needs and acceptance criteria.- Develop and maintain integrated project plans covering functional design, technical implementation, interfaces, data, testing, cutover, communication, training and operational readiness.- Manage scope, schedule, budget, quality, risks, issues, dependencies, assumptions and change control, ensuring that deviations are visible and addressed early.- Prepare concise status reporting, decisions and recommendations for LUCA governance, country stakeholders and management.Regulatory and business change delivery- Coordinate the implementation of country-specific electronic-invoicing mandates and other legal or tax-driven changes, working with Finance local, central, system implementors, and partner-system specialists.- Lead business-change projects that enhance or adapt live SAP Finance processes, ensuring alignment with the LUCA global template and the needs of productive operations.- Ensure requirements are sufficiently clear, approved and traceable, and that legal effective dates and business deadlines are translated into realistic delivery plans.- Coordinate impact assessments across SAP Finance, SAP Ariba where relevant, master data, reporting, authorizations, interfaces and non-SAP partner systems.- Protect productive operations by ensuring controlled releases, appropriate regression testing, cutover planning, support readiness and post-go-live monitoring.Functional and technical coordination- Use prior SAP Financials experience to understand end-to-end process impacts, ask informed questions and facilitate productive alignment between business and technology teams.- Coordinate solution architects, functional consultants, developers, integration teams, test teams, release management, AMS, country organizations and external partners.- Identify interdependencies across processes, systems, countries and concurrent initiatives, assign ownership and drive decisions and actions to closure.- Challenge delivery proposals, estimates and solution approaches constructively, while relying on accountable architects and specialists for detailed design authority.- Ensure project outputs are documented, supportable and handed over effectively to the relevant live-country and service-management organizations.Testing, deployment and stakeholder management- Work with LUCA Test Management to define the test approach, business participation, environments, data, entry and exit criteria, defect governance and acceptance evidence for each project.- Coordinate country UAT and business acceptance, ensuring the right stakeholders are mobilized and that open defects and residual risks are transparent before deployment.- Plan and govern cutover and production deployment activities with clear responsibilities, sequencing, readiness checks, fallback considerations and management communication.- Act as the central project contact for country Finance stakeholders, LUCA teams, METRO Digital, the System Integrator and other delivery partners.- Build trust across cultures and time zones through transparent communication, dependable follow-up, pragmatic issue resolution and timely escalation.QualificationsRequired key competencies and qualifications:- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Informatics, Information Systems, Computer Science or a related discipline.- At least 8 years of relevant experience in SAP Finance delivery, including substantial earlier experience in SAP Financials followed by a successful move into project coordination or project management.- Solid functional understanding of SAP S/4HANA Finance processes and integration points, with experience in one or more areas such as General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Asset Accounting, Controlling, tax or financial interfaces.- Proven experience delivering SAP changes or projects in a large, international and multi-country SAP landscape.- Experience managing legal, regulatory, tax, electronic-invoicing or other deadline-driven change initiatives is highly advantageous.- Experience coordinating cross-functional teams, country organizations, AMS providers, System Integrators and technology partners without relying solely on direct authority.- Experience across testing, UAT, cutover, release, deployment and hypercare in productive SAP environments.- Working knowledge of SAP Ariba, invoice-management solutions, integration platforms or partner-system landscapes is advantageous.- Confident use of project planning, collaboration and reporting tools such as Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Project, PowerPoint and Excel.- PMP, PRINCE2, Agile or SAP certification is advantageous but not required; retail or wholesale experience is beneficial.- Visible “can-do” attitude, with the energy and persistence to move complex topics understand functional and technical discussions, structure ambiguity and translate complex issues into clear actions and decisions.- Confident, articulate communication and stakeholder-management skills across business, Finance, technology, vendors and senior management.- Collaborative and culturally aware working style suited to distributed international teams and multiple country stakeholders.- Calm and solution-oriented under pressure, particularly when managing fixed legal deadlines or production-critical changes.- Excellent written and spoken English; willingness and ability to travel when required.Additional Information**What do we offer at METRO.digital?- Hybrid and agile work: thrive in a flexible, multicultural environment.At METRO.digital, we promote jobs.description: When even the smallest deviations in semiconductor manufacturing can have a significant impact, a keen eye for detail is essential. In Defect Engineering, you systematically investigate defect patterns, identify process weaknesses and contribute to the continuous improvement of our manufacturing processes and technology developments. In doing so, you combine data analysis with modern inspection methods and collaborate closely with various specialist departments.Number of positions to be filled: 2Your roleKey responsibilities in your new role- Independently handling work packages within development projects as well as in production, with a focus on identifying process weaknesses and causes of failure- Supporting the adherence to project timelines and ensuring line stability through continuous data analysis and the application of various inspection techniques- Defining inspection steps along the chip production process- Conducting and supporting experiments within development projects as well as for the implementation of process improvements- Documenting results and handing them over to production- Taking ownership of department-specific projectsYour profileYou have strong analytical skills and enjoy systematically getting to the bottom of complex technical challenges. You enjoy working in a team, exchanging knowledge with others and contributing your own ideas to improve processes and ways of working.Qualifications and skills to help you succeed- University degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics or Chemistry- Ideally 1–3 years of relevant professional experience- Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes and their interdependencies- Experience with electron microscopy and/or optical inspection and/or measurement technologies- Proficiency in both German and English#WeAreIn for driving decarbonization and digitalization.As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and IoT, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure IoT. Together, we drive innovation and customer success, while caring for our people and empowering them to reach ambitious goals. Be a part of making life easier, safer and greener.Are you in?We are on a journey to create the best Infineon for everyone.We strive to create the best Infineon for everyone by embracing diversity and inclusion. We welcome applicants for who they are and offer a workplace built on trust, openness, respect and equal opportunity.Our hiring decisions are based on skills and experience. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply.Please let your recruiter know if you need any accommodations during the interview process.Learn more about our various contact channels (https://www.infineon.com/cms/en/about-infineon/company/contacts/) and about Diversity & Inclusion (https://www.infineon.com/cms/en/careers/diversity-and-inclusion/) at Infineon.Nicole Hippmann

About AtariAtari is an interactive entertainment company and an iconic gaming industry brand recognized worldwide for its multi-platform games and licensed products. Atari owns and/or manages a portfolio of more than 400 games and franchises, including globally recognized brands such as Asteroids®, Centipede®, Missile Command®, Pong®, and RollerCoaster Tycoon®.The Atari family of brands includes Digital Eclipse, Nightdive Studios, Infogrames, AtariAge, MobyGames, as well as Hipster Whale, Coatsink, Early Morning Studios, and Stormteller Games—spanning game development, publishing, and community experiences worldwide.Atari operates internationally with offices in the US, UK, in France, Germany, Sweden, and India.About the roleMünster, Germany · Part-timeThe Executive Assistant & Project Coordinator will provide executive, administrative and project coordination support to the CFO. Based in Germany and working closely with the CFO in France, you will help keep financial administration, corporate governance and cross-border operational matters moving to completion.This is a practical coordination role for someone who is organised, persistent and comfortable following up with banks, lawyers, tax advisers, notaries, corporate service providers and internal teams. You will coordinate documents, signatures, banking administration, KYC and AML requests, legal entity changes and board formalities across the Atari Group.You do not need to be an accountant or a technical finance specialist. You do need to be reliable with sensitive information, comfortable with formal processes and willing to chase the right people until an item is complete.What you’ll do- Provide day-to-day executive and administrative support to the CFO, coordinating priorities across Germany, France and the US.- Coordinate the preparation, circulation, approval and execution of corporate documents, board resolutions, powers of attorney and other legal or finance documentation.- Manage signature workflows, monitor outstanding actions and ensure documents are signed, returned and stored on time.- Coordinate banking administration, including account openings and closures, bank mandates, signatory updates and KYC/AML requests.- Maintain accurate corporate records and legal entity documentation, ensuring information is complete, current and easy to retrieve.- Support legal entity shutdowns, entity administration and related projects by coordinating actions across Finance, Legal, tax advisers, banks and external service providers.- Liaise with banks, external legal counsel, tax lawyers, corporate service providers, notaries and local finance teams on administrative and corporate matters.- Coordinate board minutes, governance records, approvals, formalities and other recurring corporate requirements.- Support finance-related administrative work, including gathering information, tracking deadlines, maintaining records and coordinating deliverables.- Act as a project coordinator for cross-functional finance and governance workstreams, keeping owners aligned and following through on open items.- Provide administrative support for certain Luxembourg-related matters and coordinate with the relevant internal and external contacts.- Escalate delays, missing information, unclear ownership or material issues to the CFO or relevant functional lead.Requirements & Qualifications- Professional fluency in English, with the ability to communicate clearly in writing and verbally with internal and external stakeholders.- Experience in an administrative, executive support, banking, legal operations, paralegal, corporate services or similar coordination role.- Strong organisation and follow-through, with the confidence to chase people, manage deadlines and keep multiple workstreams moving.- Experience handling confidential information and formal documentation with accuracy and discretion.- Comfort working with banks, lawyers, advisers, notaries, corporate service providers or other external stakeholders.- Ability to work independently, prioritise changing requests and operate with flexibility when the CFO and key stakeholders are based in another country.- Good judgement and attention to detail when coordinating governance, KYC/AML, banking and legal entity administration.Nice to have- Professional proficiency in French.- Experience supporting a CFO, finance leader, executive team or European corporate function.- Experience in a bank, financial institution, law office, corporate services provider or multinational business.- Familiarity with KYC/AML processes, bank mandates, signatory administration, powers of attorney, board documentation or legal entity management.- Experience coordinating entity closures, corporate reorganisations, acquisitions or other cross-border projects.- Familiarity with Luxembourg corporate or finance administration.How you’ll workThis role is about making sure important administrative and governance work does not sit unresolved. You will often be coordinating several parties at once, clarifying what is needed, tracking who owns the next step and following up until the document, approval, bank request or entity action is complete.You will work closely with Finance and Legal, but you are not expected to provide accounting or legal advice. Your value will come from being dependable, organised and persistent, and from creating enough structure that the CFO and specialist advisers can make decisions and complete formalities efficiently.The role requires flexibility in working hours to accommodate cross-border coordination with the CFO in France, banks, advisers and teams in other time zones.Why join AtariThis role sits at the centre of an international finance and governance environment. You will work across Germany, France, Luxembourg and other Atari Group locations, helping coordinate the formalities and projects that support the Group’s entities and operations.You will have visibility across Finance, Legal and senior leadership, with the opportunity to build a reliable operating rhythm for corporate administration and cross-border coordination as Atari continues to integrate and develop its international business.EEO StatementAtari is an equal opportunity employer and we are committed to providing a workplace free from harassment and discrimination. We are committed to equal employment regardless of race, religion or lack thereof, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, medical condition, veteran status, ancestry, disability status, pregnancy, parental status, genetic information, political affiliation, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for severalPostdocs (2 years) (m,f,x)The Cluster of Excellence "CASA: Securing the Digital Society" is funded by DFG for the years 2026-2032 with approximately 53 million euros. CASA aims to strengthen the resilience of our digital society. The emergence of disruptive technologies in recent years, especially artificial intelligence and quantum computers, has caused substantial new challenges for cybersecurity research. In the second funding phase, CASA will specifically address these challenges. Thematic priorities include the security of quantum technologies, protection against Al-based disinformation and societal polarization, and new approaches to defending against ransomware. In addition to technical questions, it also investigates the interaction of human behavior and cybersecurity. Research at CASA, which is based at the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security, follows a strongly interdisciplinary approach. Researchers from the fields of computerscience, cryptography, electrical engineering, mathematics, and psychology work together in an unique constellation in Europe. This holistic approach is unparalleled and holds the potential for scientific breakthroughs. Ruhr-University Bochum (RUB) and its Faculty of Computer Science offer an excellent environment for aspiring young researchers. 20 years ago, the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI) was founded here. lt is now one of Europe's most prestigious institutions for basic computer security research. The HGI maintains extensive networks with leading research institutions worldwide and with media and industry. Moreover, it has produced numerous successful security startups. The pioneering work of the HGI forms the basis for the Cluster of Excellence CASA.Scope: full-timeDuration: fixed-term, 2 yearsStart: at the earliest possible dateApply by:  2026-11-09Your tasks:- Our goal is to attract postdoctoral researchers and enable them to conducttheir research with the mentorship of a PI. We expect that within the durationof this contract, candidates will be able to achieve independent achievementsin research, e.g through publications or joint research endeavours.- Therefore, we are permanently looking for excellent candidateswithoutstanding doctoral degrees in computer science, electrical engineering,mathematics and psychology (preferably with a relationship to technology) orrelated disciplines.Your profile:- An above-average doctoral degree in computer science, electricalengineering, mathematics, psychology (preferably with a relationship totechnology) or related disciplines is mandatory for the application.- Fluent spoken and written English is also required.- In addition, applicants should have basic knowledge of one or more of theresearch areas relevant to CASA: Cryptography, system security, hardwaresecurity, decentralized security, human-centered security, Al and security.- Postdoctoral students should already have published relevant papers attheleading conferences in cryptography and computer security research, aslisted e.g. at http://csrankings.org/.https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/67220716e3f3ba2e0f3fbc621a18dc39d659de040?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/67220716e3f3ba2e0f3fbc621a18dc39d659de040?ref=AfA)

jobs.occupation: IMPACT PORTFOLIO MANAGER (Fairer Futures Programmes) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description: Overview:Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.Unit’s description and purpose: The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:Role purpose: The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.Main Responsibilities:            - MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. Serve as Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact for the product-expert colleagues in Producer Networks and Global Product Teams, providing technical MEL guidance, supporting capacity on data collection and reporting, and ensuring programme MEL requirements are understood and operationalised across the system. Work with PNs to ensure that MEL frameworks for individual projects within both programme portfolios are aligned to the overarching programme frameworks, providing where capacity is available guidance and quality assurance at project inception and during implementation- Reporting, Synthesis, and Learning. Lead the preparation of programme-level MEL reporting for programmes, synthesising data and evidence from across the programme portfolio into outputs that feed into the overall strategy reporting cycle. Facilitate learning processes within programmes, identifying evidence-based insights and working with Global Product Teams and PNs to support programme adaptation where warranted. Ensure programme MEL evidence and KPI data are appropriately integrated into the overall strategy MEL cycle in close coordination with the designated strategy MEL lead within the Impact Management team.- Programme Evaluation. Lead the design, commissioning, and management of the programme evaluations. This includes developing evaluation questions in collaboration with PNs and Global Product Teams, overseeing evaluation partners, and ensuring findings are translated into actionable learning.- Impact Services and External Engagement. Identify opportunities to offer MEL technical services to Fairtrade system organisations and external partners, drawing on expertise developed through the programmes. Contribute to the scoping, design, and pitching of impact services in collaboration with the Head, with a particular focus on programme MEL, data collection design, and evaluation. Participate actively in relevant system-wide working groups, representing the Impact Management team's MEL perspective on cross-organisational initiatives.Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.SKILLS REQUIRED:Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree or higher in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years' experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning, with demonstrable experience designing and managing MEL frameworks for multi-stakeholder projects or programmes. At least two years' experience working in or with stakeholders from the Global South, preferably in agricultural or commodity supply chain contexts. Experience in coffee and bananas is an advantage.Language requirements: Fluency in English required. Professional proficiency in Spanish is a advantage. Job Specific Competencies/knowledge: - Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning- Project and Programme Management- International Development Expertise- Stakeholder Management- Planning and execution- Data Collection Design and Management- Evaluation Design and Commissioning- Enhancing data-driven decision making- Data Analysis (quantitative and qualitative)- Data Reporting and Synthesis- Capacity BuildingPersonal Qualities: - Cross-cultural communication- Facilitation- Rapid Learning- Collaboration/Teamwork- Customer Service- Presentation Skills- Relationship Management- Evidence Collecting- Flexibility- Feedback sourcingSoftware/Tools: - Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner)- Kobo Toolbox (or similar survey design and implementation tools)- Miro (or similar online whiteboarding tools)- Canva (or similar graphic design tools)- Claude.ai (or similar AI  tools)- Toladata (or similar project monitoring MEL platform)- Power BI (or similar business intelligence software)TERMS AND CONDITIONS:- This is a two-year full-time position within Fairtrade International.- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements- The office language is English.- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments starting from €5455 Gross per month- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  - 30 days of holidays per year (for fulltime employees)- Subsidised public transportation ticket- Subsidised meal services- Childcare cost subsidy Please note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

GPPP develops new ways of delivering Fairtrade’s intended impact in a changing business environment and risk context.PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:Role purpose: The Cocoa Manager is responsible for implementation of GPPP cocoa works based on work schedule agreed with the Senior Advisor Cocoa. The programme leads to farm level interventions through Small Producer Organisaitons including pruning, cocoa tree planting and shade tree planting among others. Working with Fairtrade International monitoring, evaluation and learning experts, Producer Network and National Fairtrade Organisations ensuring agreed reporting deadlines are met with quality reporting to be used with commercial stakeholders, government and other interested stakeholders.- External stakeholder engagement, traders. Traders are a critical part of the supply chain and their incorporation into the programme is desired and necessary.- External stakeholder engagement, events. Where required you will interact with media.- Fairtrade Standards and Pricing. Liaising with the lead department in Fairtrade on standards and pricing, Fairtrade’s Standards Unit and Pricing Unit, you will be working on standards and pricing matters relating to Fairtrade’s cocoa work and the programme. This will include and not limited to consultations, queries and evolution of standards and pricing. The Leibniz-Institut für Analytische Wissenschaften - ISAS - e. V. develops efficient analytical methods for health research. Thus, it contributes to the improvement of the prevention, early diagnosis, and therapy of diseases like cardiovascular diseases or cancer. Overall, the institute strives to advance precision medicine by combining knowledge from different fields such as biology, chemistry, computer science, medicine, pharmacology, and physics. ISAS is a member of the Leibniz Association and is publicly funded by the Federal Republic of Germany and its federal states.We invite applications for the Research Group Biofluorescence: PhD candidate (f/m/d)This project, funded by the DFG as part of CRC 1752, "DYNAMO: Immediate Tumor Dynamics in Melanoma Therapy“ (https://www.uni-due.de/crc1752/) seeks to combine high-resolution multi-omics profiling, advanced computational modeling, and clinically aligned biomarker stratification, in order to generate actionable, patient-specific predictions and resistance-targeting interventions in melanoma therapy. You will be responsible for finding out the role of neutrophils for the early development of therapy resistance in human melanoma. The project is being carried out in collaboration with University Hospital Essen and the University of Duisburg-Essen.You will be responsible for- Experimental setup and execution of neutrophil functional profiling in the context of melanoma immune regulation and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response- Functional assays of neutrophils including migration, phagocytosis, and ROS production- Optimization and standardization of neutrophil functional assays for primary human samples- Few-cell proteomics for deep molecular characterization of neutrophil subsets- Multicolor flow cytometry of PBMCs and immune cell populations- Live-cell imaging and advanced microscopy for dynamic immune cell behavior analysis- Planning and execution of stimulation and inhibition experiments to dissect signaling pathways regulating neutrophil function in the melanoma context- Data processing, analysis, interpretation, and visualization of experimental results in collaboration with computational partnersYour profile- Completed diploma or master’s degree in molecular biology, cancer biology, immunology, cell biology, bioinformatics, translational medicine or related disciplines- Experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques, ideally with hands-on experience with functional immune cell assays (preferably with neutrophils or myeloid cells) is an advantage- Strong interest in melanoma biology, tumor immunology, immune checkpoint therapy, translational cancer research, and tumor–immune interactions- Experience with cell culture, flow cytometry, microscopy, proteomics workflows or high-dimensional immune profiling approaches is desirable- Experience with bioinformatics or biostatistics is beneficial but not required- Ability to work independently and in interdisciplinary teams, with strong organizational skills and analytical thinking- High level of self-motivation, scientific curiosity, reliability, creativity, and team-oriented personality with enthusiasm to work in a collaborative research environment- Fluent in spoken and written EnglishWe offer- A clear research topic as well as multifold training and support for PhD students in framework of ISAS and the Leibniz association- Opportunities for scientific training and development in an international environment and an excellent working atmosphere in a very dynamic and professional team- Access to state-of-the-art technologies including few-cell proteomics, high-dimensional flow cytometry, and advanced microscopy platforms- Integration into an interdisciplinary, internationally visible, translation-oriented cancer immunology research network- The opportunity to present your data on international conferences and participate in workshops- A wide range of opportunities for further training and qualifications- Flexible working times, mobile working and attractive social benefits- Family-friendly infrastructure and support from a family serviceNon-residents who apply for this job will receive help from the institute to find accommodation and to handle authorities. Applications from disabled applicants are welcome. ISAS supports the principle of equal opportunity for all employees and therefore particularly encourages women to apply.The part-time position (65%) starts on October 1, 2026, and is offered until June 30, 2030. The salary will be according to the German TV-L and falls within the pay group 13. The time limitation of the contract is based on the Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz (WissZeitVG).ISAS collects and processes the personal data of its applicants in accordance with European and German legal regulations. The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.The following full-/part-time position (38.5/19.5 hours per week)  is to be filled as soon as possible in the Institute for Hygiene and Public Health, Section Global Child Health of the University Hospital Bonn:Scientific coordinator (m/f/d)The Section of Global Child Health was established in November 2025 with the appointment of the Endowed Professorship in Global Child Health. The Section’s remit includes research and teaching in Germany and internationally, as well as clinical practice and the applied, practice-oriented engagement with global health challenges affecting children and adolescents. The professorship is structured as a tandem appointment with a corresponding position at the University of Malawi, based in Lilongwe.You will work in close collaboration with the section head in establishing sound research and communication networks with partners in Malawi and GermanyThe professorship focuses on research in the area of neonatal, child, and adolescent health in “Low and Middle Income Countries” (LMICs), identifies barriers to and solutions for improving global child health, and facilitates the transfer of epidemiological and clinical evidence into health care services with the goal of improving the health status of all children globally.It facilitates institutional, national and international networking and collaboration with universities, academic institutions and key development partners.In addition, it provides academic and health policy advice to national and international governmental as well as non-governmental organizations with regard to global child health.The position is initially limited to three years and remunerated according to TV-L EG 13 (German tax ID is a prerequisite). Subject to interest and feasibility, a temporary increase in the scope of employment through third-party funded resources is envisaged.Tasks:This position offers the opportunity to actively contribute to the development of global strategies for improving children's health and to build and design a completely new international research and education structure.- Strategic coordination and management of international research, education and clinical programmes across the two professorships and the EKFS network- Planning, coordination, and monitoring of cross-institutional activities with academic and non-academic partners- Management of communication channels between institutions, disciplines, and countries, ensuring efficient information flow and alignment of activities- Coordination, and implementation of training materials and structured capacity-building programmes in collaboration with international experts- Planning, organisation, and delivery of international workshops and seminars in online and on-site formats- Preparation of annual progress and impact reports, dissemination of results through conferences and other scientific communication formats- Contribution to the contexts- Strong teamwork skills, resilience, and the ability to assert and represent set positions- Full professional proficiency in both German and English, written and spoken Willingness to maintain an appropriate on-site presence at the university in Bonn- Previous extended study, research, or professional experience in a low- or middle-income country would be considered a strong
